audience: AI coding agents and automation tools that need to discover how to use Canary without loading the full documentation corpus.

format.query_language: Canary query path syntax: whole object with '.', dotted object keys, bracketed object keys, and list indexes. This is not jq.
format.progressive_disclosure: Top-level objects are compact indexes. Query deeper paths for operational details.

overview.what_is_canary: Canary is a Python-based workflow and test execution framework for defining, scheduling, running, and inspecting computational jobs across environments ranging from developer laptops to HPC systems.
overview.core_model: Canary core executes Job objects. It does not require one universal job-definition file format. Job generators interpret user-facing definitions and emit JobSpecIR or JobSpec objects. Canary resolves dependencies, constructs Jobs for a Session, schedules them with resources, runs them, and persists results.
when_to_use: Run computational tests or simulations with structured status, logs, artifacts, and measurements.
Define parameter sweeps and dependency-aware workflows.
Execute jobs locally, under HPC batching integrations, or through extension-provided execution backends.
Expose structured results to scripts, CI systems, reports, or AI agents.

major_concepts.job_generator: Interprets an input representation such as .pyt, .vvt, CTest metadata, YAML, or another domain-specific format and emits JobSpecIR or JobSpec objects.
major_concepts.jobspec: A resolved description of a job: identity, command, parameters, resources, dependencies, assets, artifacts, and metadata.
major_concepts.job: A concrete session execution object constructed from a JobSpec and consumed by Canary's scheduler/executor.
major_concepts.session: A persistent execution run containing jobs, session metadata, measurements, and a session.lock manifest.
major_concepts.workspace: A persistent .canary directory containing specs, sessions, logs, cache, reports, a SQLite index, and temporary state.
major_concepts.resource_pool: Topology-aware model of available resources, organized by nodes and resource instances with slots.
major_concepts.query: A lightweight JSON path query command for job locks, session locks, and static capability datasets.

pipeline.summary: Canary separates user-facing job definitions from execution. Generators create specs; the workspace resolves and stores specs; sessions construct jobs; the executor runs jobs and persists results.

stages.name: definition
stages.description: A user writes or supplies a job definition in a format understood by an installed generator.

stages.name: generation
stages.description: A Job Generator emits JobSpecIR or JobSpec objects.

stages.name: dependency_resolution
stages.description: Dependency selectors are resolved into concrete SpecDependency edges.

stages.name: selection
stages.description: Rules filter or mask specs by keyword, parameters, owner, regex, path, IDs, resources, or rerun state.

stages.name: session_construction
stages.description: A Workspace constructs Job objects from JobSpec objects for a Session.

stages.name: execution
stages.description: A resource-aware queue schedules runnable jobs. Launchers execute job commands and update status, timekeeper, and measurements.

stages.name: persistence
stages.description: Job lock files, session lock files, artifacts, logs, and a SQLite index persist execution state.

pipeline.important_distinction: Canary core does not parse every supported job-definition format. Generators own input formats; Canary core owns execution of Jobs.

JobSpecIR.purpose: Intermediate generator output that may contain unresolved dependency selectors.

JobSpec.purpose: Resolved job specification with concrete dependency edges.

Job.purpose: Concrete execution object in a Session.

Generator.purpose: Discovers/interprets user job definitions and emits specs.
Generator.reference_implementation: The Python job definition package, commonly exposed through .pyt files, is the reference generator implementation.

status_model.category: Broad category such as PASS, FAIL, SKIP, CANCEL, or NONE.
status_model.outcome: Specific outcome such as SUCCESS, FAILED, DIFFED, TIMEOUT, SKIPPED, BLOCKED, ERROR, BROKEN, XFAIL, XDIFF, CANCELLED, or INTERRUPTED.
status_model.reason: Human-readable reason, usually populated for non-success outcomes.

persistence.summary: Persistence is hybrid. SQLite is an index/result/state store. Lock files and the filesystem are authoritative for detailed serialized job/session state and artifacts.
persistence.sqlite: workspace.sqlite3 stores specs, spec metadata, dependencies, selections, selection metadata, and latest/history result rows.
persistence.job_lock: Each executed job writes testcase.lock in its execution directory.
persistence.session_lock: Each session writes session.lock in its session directory.
persistence.artifacts: Outputs, linked/copied assets, logs, and artifacts live in job work directories and optionally in views or reports.
persistence.result_spool: Completed jobs are spooled through a filesystem queue so the parent process can write results to SQLite.

tests.summary: Canary tests are jobs produced by generators. The reference authoring format is provided by the Python job definition package, but other generators may define other input formats.

authoring.reference_format: Python job definitions are commonly written as .pyt files interpreted by the canary_pyt generator.
minimal_pattern: Place generator directives at module scope.
Place executable test logic in a function.
Exit with code 0 for success or use Canary exceptions/exit statuses for structured outcomes.
authoring.important_distinction: This Python format is a generator-provided format, not a requirement imposed by Canary core.

directives.purpose: Directives communicate generation-time information to a generator.
directives.reference: Use canary query -c capabilities .commands.reference and generated directive reference pages for exact syntax.

common.parameterize: Generate multiple job instances from parameter values.
common.depends_on: Declare dependencies by name, pattern, or structured selector.
common.copy: Copy an asset into the execution directory.
common.link: Symlink an asset into the execution directory.
common.artifact: Declare files to preserve or report.
common.cpus: Set fixed CPU resource requirement without creating a named parameter variation.
common.gpus: Set fixed GPU resource requirement without creating a named parameter variation.
common.xfail: Mark job as expected to fail.
common.xdiff: Mark job as expected to diff.
common.skipif: Skip jobs conditionally with a reason.
common.set_id: Assign stable explicit IDs for generated specs.

parameters.purpose: Parameters create job variants, participate in naming, and may define resource requirements when names match resource types.
resource_parameters: any parameter name matching a resource type in the resource pool
common_mistakes: Using a resource-like parameter without defining that resource type in the resource pool.
Assuming cpus(arg) changes the job display name; fixed resource directives set meta-parameters and do not create named variants.
Duplicating keys between parameters and meta_parameters.

assets_and_artifacts.assets: Files or directories staged into the job workspace by copy, link, or none actions.
assets_and_artifacts.artifacts: Files collected or exposed after execution depending on status.

expected_outcomes.failed: Unhandled nonzero exit codes usually map to FAILED.
expected_outcomes.skipped: Use Canary skip exit status or TestSkipped.
expected_outcomes.diffed: Use Canary diff exit status or TestDiffed.
expected_outcomes.timeout: A job exceeding its timeout is marked TIMEOUT.
expected_outcomes.xfail: Expected nonzero exit is marked XFAIL when configured.
expected_outcomes.xdiff: Expected diff is marked XDIFF when configured.

workflows.summary: A Canary workflow is a dependency-aware collection of generated jobs executed within a session.

steps: Choose or implement a generator for the job-definition format.
Write job definitions with commands, parameters, resources, dependencies, assets, and artifacts.
Select jobs by paths, tags, keywords, parameters, owners, regex, or IDs.
Run selected jobs in a session.
Inspect structured results, logs, artifacts, and reports.

dependency_workflows.description: Dependencies allow jobs to run only after upstream jobs complete with required outcomes.
dependency_workflows.rerun_closure: Rerun logic includes downstream jobs that depend on selected roots and may include upstream jobs masked as already satisfied.

post_processing.description: Post-processing can be implemented inside a generated job, as a composite/analysis job, or in post-test/session hooks.
post_processing.recommended_for_agents: Emit structured measurements with Job.add_measurement or Session.add_measurement so post-processing results can be queried without log scraping.

jobs.summary: A Job is a concrete execution object in a session. It wraps a JobSpec, an ExecutionSpace, dependency Job objects, status, lifecycle state, timekeeper, measurements, variables, and resource allocation.

important_fields.workspace: ExecutionSpace with root, relative path, and session.
important_fields.dependencies: List of Dependency objects pointing to upstream Jobs.
important_fields.measurements: Structured key/value data recorded during execution.
important_fields.variables: Runtime environment variables passed to the job.

measurement_api.storage: Serialized into testcase.lock and result records.

readiness.is_ready: True when all dependencies are done and satisfied.
readiness.is_runnable: False when done, skipped, or permanently blocked by failed dependency criteria.
readiness.blocked: A job can be marked BLOCKED when a dependency finishes with an outcome that does not satisfy its dependency condition.

sessions.summary: A Session is a persistent execution run containing jobs, session name, prefix directory, measurements, job IDs, start/finish timestamps, and return code.

lifecycle.run: Session.run constructs a Runner for runnable jobs and invokes canary_runtests.

sessions.latest: The workspace refs/latest file points to the latest session directory.

resources.summary: Canary uses a topology-aware ResourcePool to prevent oversubscription and to assign runtime resource IDs to jobs.

job_requests.source: Job.required_resources returns a list of NodeRequest objects derived from JobSpec resource parameters.
job_requests.nodes: A nodes parameter greater than 1 creates multiple per-node requests and treats multi-node jobs as whole-node reservations.

runtime_environment.template_expansion: Existing job variables may use %(cpu_ids)s or %(gpu_ids)s style placeholders that are expanded after resource assignment.

dependencies.summary: Dependencies are declared by generators as selectors and resolved into concrete SpecDependency edges between JobSpecs.

fields.pattern: Name, full name, file path, ID, or glob pattern to match.
fields.expects: Expected match count: '+', '?', '*', or a positive integer.
fields.when: Condition required for dependent job to run.

conditions.on_success: Dependency status category must be PASS.
conditions.on_failure: Dependency status category must be FAIL.
conditions.always: Dependency only needs to be done.
conditions.*: Alias for always in some generator inputs.
conditions.expression: Other strings may be evaluated as simple status/category expressions.

common_mistakes: Forgetting that dependencies match generated job names after parameter expansion.
Expecting a downstream job to run when an upstream dependency failed but the condition is on_success.

local.summary: Local execution uses a ResourceQueue and ResourceQueueExecutor to run jobs in worker processes while respecting dependencies and resource capacity.
local.workers: The --workers option controls the maximum process pool size, but resource availability may further limit concurrency.
local.launcher: The default launcher runs the job command as a subprocess in the job workspace.

hpc.summary: HPC execution is provided by extension packages and typically batches jobs for submission through hpc_connect.

timeouts.job_timeout: Job.total_timeout applies configured multipliers to the JobSpec timeout.
timeouts.session_timeout: A session timeout may terminate all in-flight jobs.
timeouts.launcher_timeout: The default subprocess launcher kills the process group on timeout.

query.summary: canary query inspects JSON data from job locks, session locks, or static capability datasets.

selectors.-j, --job: Query testcase.lock for a job found by ID or matching spec.
selectors.-s, --session: Query session.lock for a session name or prefix; latest is supported.
selectors.-c, --capabilities: Query a named static capability dataset, such as capabilities.

query.not_jq: The query language is intentionally small. It does not support filters, pipes, recursive descent, expressions, or transformations.

hooks.summary: Canary extensions use pluggy hooks to add commands, generators, resource behavior, launchers, runtime behavior, reports, measurements, and lifecycle actions.

canary_sessionstart.purpose: Runs when a new session starts.
canary_sessionstart.agent_use: Attach session-level structured metadata with session.add_measurement.

canary_runteststart.purpose: Runs during job setup before the job command executes.
canary_runteststart.default_behavior: The built-in wrapper calls case.setup() and then saves the job.
canary_runteststart.agent_use: Prepare generated inputs, validate preconditions, or record setup metadata.

canary_runtest.purpose: Runs the test body or launcher for a Job.
canary_runtest.default_behavior: The built-in wrapper calls case.run() and saves the job.
canary_runtest.agent_use: Can be extended for custom execution behavior, but launchers are usually preferable for changing process execution.

canary_runtest_finish.purpose: Runs after the test execution phase and before the job is finally saved.
canary_runtest_finish.default_behavior: The built-in wrapper calls case.finish() and saves the job.
canary_runtest_finish.agent_use: Inspect outputs, perform post-processing, add measurements, and attach metadata.

canary_runtests_report.purpose: Runs after a test session to generate reports or summaries.
canary_runtests_report.agent_use: Create machine-readable reports or summarize structured measurements.

canary_sessionfinish.purpose: Runs after a non-reused session finishes.
canary_sessionfinish.agent_use: Add final session metadata, archive outputs, notify external systems, or trigger follow-on automation.

generation.canary_collectstart: Register job generator classes with the collector.
generation.canary_generate_modifyitems: Inspect or mutate generated JobSpecs before they are stored or run.

execution.canary_runtests: Override or provide a test-session execution backend.
execution.canary_runtest_launcher: Return a Launcher for an individual Job.

resources.canary_resource_pool_update: Mutate or augment a ResourcePool before use.
resources.canary_resource_pool_accommodates: Determine whether a Job can be accommodated.

results.summary: Canary records status, lifecycle timing, measurements, logs, artifacts, views, and reports.

logs.stderr_default: stderr is combined with stdout unless configured otherwise

views.purpose: Expose latest results in a user-facing tree.

reports.junit: JUnit XML report for CI systems.
reports.html: Static HTML report with job pages and file browser.

commands.summary: Use generated command reference pages for exact syntax. This object provides agent-oriented command selection guidance.
commands.reference: Run canary query -c capabilities .commands.<name> for concise purpose and common use.

collect.purpose: Find generators and cache generated specs in a workspace.

select.purpose: Create, rename, delete, or derive tagged selections.

find.purpose: Discover and display generated specs without necessarily storing/running them.

status.purpose: Inspect job status in a workspace.

log.purpose: Display session or job log files.

location.purpose: Print input, log, working, or source locations for a job/spec.

query.purpose: Query job locks, session locks, or static capability datasets as JSON.

report.purpose: Create reports from stored Canary results.

plugins.summary: Canary functionality is extended with pluggy plugins registered through the existing canary entry point group.

generators.purpose: Add support for new job-definition formats.

configuration.purpose: Add configuration sections and command-line options.

launchers.purpose: Control how a job command is executed.

reporters.purpose: Generate structured reports from jobs and sessions.

documentation.purpose: Extension packages can provide docs by including a docs/index.rst directory inside the package associated with a canary entry point.
documentation.build_mechanism: The docs build script discovers canary entry points, checks for docs/index.rst, creates include stubs, and includes them in the Sphinx build.

hpc.purpose: Batch jobs and submit them to HPC schedulers through hpc_connect.

skills.summary: Canary ships small agent-facing skills as installed package data. Skills provide procedural guidance and point agents to targeted capability queries. The capabilities database remains the detailed factual reference.
intended_agent_flow: Use a Canary skill for procedural guidance.
When detailed facts are needed, query canary query -c TOPIC.
Prefer targeted topics such as overview, tests, hooks.post, query, resources, plugins, or agent_workflows.
Use canary query -c all only when broad knowledge of the entire capability database is required.

bundled_skills.canary-orientation: General orientation: what Canary is, when to use it, and where to query for more detail.
bundled_skills.canary-test-authoring: Authoring and modifying Canary tests/job definitions.
bundled_skills.canary-run-debug: Running jobs, inspecting status, querying state, and debugging failures.
bundled_skills.canary-workflows-results: Workflow orchestration, structured measurements, post-processing, and reports.
bundled_skills.canary-extension-development: Developing generators, hooks, plugins, launchers, reporters, resource integrations, and extension docs.

agent_workflows.summary: Agents can use Canary as a structured execution and observation layer for code development, testing, simulation, and post-processing.
principles: Use Canary commands to execute work instead of manually orchestrating subprocesses when dependencies, resources, persistence, or reports matter.
Prefer structured measurements over log scraping.
Use canary query to retrieve state and measurements.
Use hooks or generator metadata to attach domain-specific data.
Use selections and rerun strategies to minimize repeated work.
basic_loop: Run canary run PATH or canary run TAG.
Query structured data with canary query.
Use measurements and statuses to decide next action.
measurement_loop: A test or hook records a measurement using Job.add_measurement.
A session hook records workflow metadata using Session.add_measurement.
The agent queries the measurement with canary query.
The agent uses the result to update code, inputs, or workflow state.
common_mistakes: Scraping canary-out.txt for data that could be emitted as a structured measurement.
Assuming .pyt is the only way to define jobs.
Ignoring dependency outcomes when interpreting skipped or blocked jobs.
Assuming SQLite contains every artifact or full serialized job state.
Changing resource requirements without checking the resource pool.

workspace_layout..canary/tmp: Temporary files including result spool data.

query: The query command is intentionally lightweight and not a jq-compatible query engine.
It reads JSON-like lock or static dataset objects and applies simple path selection.
capabilities_database: The capabilities database is static and may summarize behavior rather than describe every option.
Generated command/directive reference remains the authority for exact command-line and directive syntax.
Python API docs remain the authority for full method signatures.
documentation: Extension documentation is included only for installed packages that have a canary entry point and a docs/index.rst file.
